rationale: Section 2.4 expressly conditions the identification, decision rights, terms, and additional cost approvals for a Marketer on action by the JPT "or otherwise in accordance with Section 2.1," while Section 2.1 assigns Marketer selection under Section 2.4 to the JPT without completing the JPT's decision-making rules in the excerpt.

Section 1.8 defines "Development Plan" solely by reference to Section 2.1, under which the Development Plan is a future written Exhibit A that CARDAX and CAPSUGEL "will agree upon" and administer through the JPT.

Section 3.8 requires CARDAX to use "Commercially Reasonable Efforts" for freedom-to-operate assessments, which through Section 1.7's definition allows CARDAX to weigh profitability, marketplace competitiveness, and proprietary position rather than imposing an absolute clearance duty.

Section 3(c) limits post-termination survival to "representations, warranties and indemnities," omitting Section 4 and leaving unclear whether invoices due 30 days after receipt under Section 4(a), taxes arising out of the Agreement under Section 4(b), and late-payment interest under Section 4(c) survive expiration or termination.

Section 3(c) restricts survival after expiration or termination to "representations, warranties and indemnities," omitting Section 6 and creating a material gap over whether obligations protecting Confidential Information and Trade Secrets disclosed "during the term hereof" under Section 6(a)-(b) cease upon termination.
